# Greek-Owned Cargo Ship Sinks After Three Naval Drones Strike Vessel Near Bulgaria

SEO Title: Greek Cargo Ship Sinks After Three Drone Strikes in Black Sea Near Bulgaria

Meta Description: A Greek-owned container ship carrying 421 containers has sunk after three naval drones struck it near Bulgaria's Black Sea coast. All 18 crew members were rescued.

Excerpt: A Greek-owned cargo vessel has sunk after being struck by three naval drones in the Black Sea near Bulgaria. All 18 crew members survived, while authorities investigate the attack and its possible connection to the Russia-Ukraine war.

## Cargo Ship Sinks Following Drone Attack

A Greek-owned container ship has sunk in the Black Sea after being struck by three naval drones near Bulgaria's coastline.

The incident occurred on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, involving a Liberian-flagged vessel known as Contship Jet.

The ship was reportedly carrying 421 containers when it was attacked while travelling through Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone.

According to Bulgarian authorities, the vessel suffered significant damage and eventually sank.

The attack has raised further concerns about the safety of international commercial shipping in the Black Sea, particularly as tensions surrounding the Russia-Ukraine war continue.

## All 18 Crew Members Rescued

Despite the severity of the attack, all 18 people aboard the vessel survived.

The crew consisted of 14 Filipino nationals and four Ukrainian nationals.

Following the incident, Bulgarian rescue teams transferred the crew members to the port city of Varna.

Contships Management confirmed that everyone aboard had been rescued safely.

The successful rescue operation prevented the incident from becoming another major maritime loss of life.

## What Was the Ship Carrying?

The Contship Jet was transporting 421 containers on its journey from Haifa in Israel to Constanta in Romania.

Its cargo reportedly included lithium-ion batteries, corrosive liquids, acids and industrial components.

Because of the nature of some of the materials aboard, authorities had to assess whether the sinking could create an environmental threat.

Initial inspections carried out by Bulgarian authorities reportedly found no visible evidence of pollution from the vessel.

However, continued monitoring remained important because damaged containers and industrial chemicals can create environmental risks when they enter marine environments.

## Who Was Behind the Drone Attack?

As of the initial reports, responsibility for the attack had not been established.

Authorities did not immediately identify the organisation or country responsible for launching the naval drones.

The incident occurred against the background of Russia's ongoing war in Ukraine, which has increasingly affected maritime security in the western Black Sea.

According to reporting by Reuters, the Contship Jet was among several vessels targeted in drone attacks near Bulgaria during October.

The Bulgarian government said at least six ships had been attacked in the area during the month.

The incidents have increased pressure on authorities to improve maritime security.

## Why Is Bulgaria Concerned?

Bulgaria is a member of both the European Union and NATO.

Its Black Sea coastline is strategically important for international trade, energy transportation and regional security.

Repeated attacks on commercial vessels could affect shipping confidence and increase the cost of transporting goods through the region.

Bulgarian naval commander Kiril Mihaylov said authorities had received information about a possible drone attack from a French patrol aircraft but were unable to prevent the strike.

The government has since sought additional assistance to strengthen security along its Black Sea coastline.

## Could the Attack Affect International Shipping?

The Black Sea is an important route for transporting agricultural products, industrial materials, energy resources and other commercial goods.

When ships become targets of military attacks, shipping companies may reconsider their routes or demand additional security arrangements.

Insurance costs can also increase when vessels operate in areas considered dangerous.

Repeated attacks could therefore affect businesses and consumers beyond the countries directly involved in the conflict.

For international shipping companies, the incident is another reminder of the risks associated with operating in conflict-affected maritime regions.

## What Happens Next?

Bulgarian authorities are expected to continue investigating the circumstances surrounding the attack and monitoring the environmental impact of the sinking.

International attention will also focus on whether further attacks occur in the western Black Sea.

Although all 18 crew members survived, the loss of the Contship Jet highlights the growing risks facing commercial shipping near the Russia-Ukraine conflict zone.

The incident has renewed calls for stronger maritime protection and improved coordination between countries operating in the Black Sea region.
